title: Export Market Analysis
quiz.0.question: Measured by export "value", which is the largest single market for Italian wine?
quiz.0.explanation: The US is the largest market for Italian wine by value, with huge demand for Super Tuscans and Barolo as well as Prosecco and Pinot Grigio, accounting for about a quarter of Italy's wine export value.
quiz.1.question: Which sparkling-wine category does Italy export in the greatest volume?
quiz.1.explanation: Prosecco is the sparkling wine Italy exports in the greatest volume and one of the world's best-selling sparkling wines, made mainly as Prosecco DOC in the Veneto and Friuli, with Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG at the top.
quiz.2.question: Measured by export "volume", which country is usually the largest importer of Italian wine?
quiz.2.explanation: Germany is the largest market for Italian wine by volume, mainly importing inexpensive bulk and everyday wines — a large share by volume but a lower average price.
quiz.3.question: Which Italian region is the main source of Prosecco, the world's best-selling sparkling wine?
quiz.3.explanation: The Veneto is the main source of Prosecco; in particular Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore DOCG is the top area and the core engine of Italian sparkling exports.
slides.0.title: Export Market Analysis
slides.0.subtitle: Italian wine's global map: key markets, best-selling products and future opportunities
slides.1.title: Italian Wine Exports at a Glance
slides.1.content:
Italy is a major global wine exporter, selling about half of its production on international markets. Its export map stretches from mature markets in Europe and North America to fast-growing Asia, forming a diversified global footprint. Understanding each market is key to grasping the global competitiveness of Italian wine.

>€7bnin annual exports, among the world's top two for many years
~50%of production exported, highly dependent on international markets
USAlargest export market "by value"
Germanylargest export market "by volume"
slides.2.title: The Four Key Export Markets
slides.2.content:
🇺🇸 United States (largest by value)

About a quarter of export value

Favours Pinot Grigio, Prosecco, Chianti and top Super Tuscans; strong premium demand; Italy's most important destination for fine wine

🇩🇪 Germany (largest by volume)

First by volume, but a lower average price

Mainly imports inexpensive bulk and everyday wines; wins on quantity; Italian wine takes a very large share of German supermarket shelves

🇬🇧 United Kingdom (mature, stable market)

Strong demand for Prosecco and traditional reds

Import formalities increased after Brexit but basic demand is solid; a mature sommelier culture that values Italian fine wine highly

🌏 Asia (the most promising emerging market)

China, Japan and Korea growing fast

A strong affinity for Italian culture and food; a smaller share than Europe and North America for now, but the fastest growth; the Italian wine industry is actively promoting native grapes and food-and-wine culture
slides.3.title: Italy's Four Key Export Products
slides.3.content:
The core of Italy's export success is a handful of "global star products", each clearly positioned and covering different consumer tiers

🥂 Prosecco (Veneto): one of the world's best-selling sparkling wines, made by the Charmat method, fresh, easy and affordable. It drives the image of Italian sparkling exports and is at the heart of Aperol Spritz culture
🍋 Pinot Grigio (northern Italy): one of the world's most popular light whites, especially strong in the US. Santa Margherita succeeded in making it a byword for premium everyday white
🍷 Chianti (Toscana): Italian wine's "goodwill ambassador", the most widespread in the mid-price range. Chianti Classico with its black rooster (Gallo Nero) emblem is an entry point to the world of Italian wine
👑 Barolo / Super Tuscans: the benchmarks of the premium market, driving Italian wine's brand upgrade. Sassicaia and Ornellaia are active at international auctions, and single-vineyard Barolo MGAs are sought after by collectors
slides.4.title: Market Challenges and Opportunities
slides.4.content:
Although Italian wine holds a strong position on the global market, it faces a complex mix of structural challenges and new opportunities.

⚠️ Main challenges

  • Slower growth in mature markets: traditional markets such as the US, Germany and the UK are nearing saturation, with competition from France, Spain, Chile, Argentina and others
  • Falling domestic consumption: per-capita consumption in Italy has fallen from about 100 litres in the 1970s to about 40 litres, so the industry depends heavily on exports
  • Brand fragmentation: tens of thousands of small estates act alone, with no systematic national marketing, making a unified global image hard to build
  • Hard-to-remember names: the Denominazione system (DOCG/DOC) is complex and hard for consumers to remember, affecting purchase decisions

✅ Key opportunities

  • The rise of Asia: China, Japan and Korea's strong affinity for Italian food and culture makes them the most promising growth markets of the next decade
  • Premiumisation: the global middle class is willing to pay more for quality Italian wine, and the fine-wine market keeps expanding
  • Organic and sustainability: Italy's share of organic vineyards is among the world's highest, matching consumers' health awareness — a competitive advantage
  • Exporting aperitivo culture: Aperol Spritz and Negroni cocktail culture has swept the world, boosting exports of Prosecco and Italian bitter aperitifs
slides.5.title: Key Takeaways
slides.5.points.0: Italy exports over €7 billion of wine a year, selling about half of its production on international markets
slides.5.points.1: The US is Italy's largest market "by value", with huge demand for Prosecco, Pinot Grigio and Super Tuscans
slides.5.points.2: Germany is Italy's largest market "by volume", mainly importing inexpensive everyday and bulk wines
slides.5.points.3: The UK market is mature and stable, with Prosecco and Chianti as the two mainstays; formalities increased after Brexit but demand is solid
slides.5.points.4: Asia (China, Japan, Korea) is the fastest-growing emerging market, with a strong affinity for Italian food culture
slides.5.points.5: Prosecco is the sparkling wine exported in the greatest volume, made mainly in the Veneto; Pinot Grigio is the most popular light white
slides.5.points.6: Chianti is the most popular export red; Barolo and the Super Tuscans are the flagship image products of the premium market
slides.5.points.7: The Italian wine industry's biggest structural challenge is brand fragmentation; its biggest opportunities are Asia and premiumisation
